engagement_title: Meridian Summit delegate badges: bring eighteen self-submitted portraits to one registration wall, recover the summit mark off the lectern plate, rebuild the bureau's badge into a live run, and hand back the room set editable
vertical: Events, Conferences and Promotion, an invitation-only two-day executive summit for regional transmission operators, infrastructure investors and utility policy staff (Providence, Rhode Island)
real_brief_anchor: The batch ledger carries no quoted posting for this slot, so the anchor here is the recurring posted-job shape rather than one quoted advertisement. Primary anchor: the Upwork commission repeatedly listed as 'InDesign data merge for conference name badges, roster CSV plus per-attendee headshots', posted by event organisers who hold last year's badge only as a flat print file from the venue's print bureau, have no working file and nobody who remembers how it was built, and need this year's roster, organisations, tracks and photographs put through the same badge, delivered as one ordered press file for the on-site printer plus individual files for the reprint desk. Co-anchor: the Upwork and Freelancer.com 'event collateral designer, badges plus registration signage plus closing deck' listings, which bundle the badge run with the registration-desk board, the session-room door cards and the closing slides, because organisers buy the room as one job and never the badge alone. Laundered to the fictional Meridian Council and its Meridian Summit; no real company, person, venue, sponsor or trademark appears. The ledger recorded this slot as a badge merge and nothing else, which is one surface and one deliverable class. LAYOUT-23 restores the commission the organisers actually post: eighteen portraits taken by eighteen different people have to be made into one wall before any of them binds, the summit mark has to be recovered because nobody kept the file, and the badge run, the registration board and the closing slides all have to agree with each other in a room where every delegate paid twenty-four hundred dollars to be there.
client_one_liner: Eighteen delegates, eighteen photographs taken by eighteen different people, a badge the venue bureau made last year off a file we do not have, and a registration desk that opens in five weeks.
client_brief:
Meridian Summit, delegate badges and the room set.

Meridian Council runs one closed-door executive summit a year. Two days, eighteen seats, twenty-four hundred dollars a seat, and the people in the room either run regional transmission networks or write the cheques that rebuild them. Everything they touch at the venue has to feel like it cost what they paid for it.

The badges worry me most. Last year the venue's print bureau made them from a file we no longer have and nobody here knows how it was put together. Keep the badge exactly as it looks, it is what people expect. What changes is what is on it: this year's delegate, their organisation, their track and their own photograph.

The photographs are the mess. Everybody sent their own. Some are proper studio headshots, some are cropped out of a conference photo, one is plainly a phone picture in a hotel corridor. Standing at the registration wall they have to look like they were all taken for us: same treatment, same framing, faces sitting the same way in the frame, and skin that looks like the person's actual skin rather than everybody averaged into one colour.

Names and organisations exactly as people registered them. Nothing shortened, nothing abbreviated, no post-nominals dropped. For half this room the title is the reason they are in it.

The check-in desk scans people in, so each badge needs its own code.

Our mark is on the badge. The only clean version I can find anywhere is a photograph of the brass plate on the lectern from last year. Pull it off that and use the same one on everything.

Three things we do not have at all: the board behind the registration desk, the door cards for the two session rooms, and the closing slides. Give those back as one file we can edit, because the running order moves the week before.

Send the badge run to the printer as one ordered file, plus one file per delegate for the reprint desk. And if anything in our registration export looks wrong to you, say so before it prints.
price_band_and_audience: Twenty-four hundred dollars a seat, eighteen seats, invitation only. Delegates are 40 to 65, they run regional transmission networks, sit on infrastructure funds or write utility policy, and they have been to two hundred conferences. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct badge is heavy, quiet and photo-forward: one restrained neutral, generous space, the name set large and calm, the organisation smaller but complete, the track carried as a small typographic distinction rather than a shouted colour block, and the portrait treated like a portrait. Push it toward the bright, playful, colour-blocked, text-only badge that a free two-hundred-person community meetup correctly uses and the delegate reads it as a name sticker, which at this price is an insult they will mention to the person who invited them. Push it the other way into a decorated or celebratory register and it reads as a gala rather than a closed-door working session. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,600 to 3,200 dollars fixed, or 45 to 75 dollars an hour across 30 to 45 hours.

brand_identity.tagline: The people who run the grid, and the people who fund it.

brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no working file for the badge; last year's was made by the venue's print bureau from artwork nobody kept. The only clean version of the summit mark that survives is the engraving on the brass lectern plate, photographed under the room's downlights. The registration board, the two session door cards and the closing slides do not exist yet.
brand_identity.values: Names and organisations exactly as registered, nothing shortened or abbreviated, and restraint carried as the signal of credibility.

assets_supplied.name: delegate_headshots/ (18 files, 900 x 1200 to 4200 x 5600)
assets_supplied.kind: Self-submitted portraits, one per delegate, collected through the registration form. Studio headshots, crops out of group photographs, and one phone picture taken in a hotel corridor.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everyone sent their own. Some are proper, some are not. They have to look like they were all taken for us."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Five portraits sit within a whisker of their own background in value (a light grey jacket on a pale grey sweep, platinum hair against cream, a white shirt against a white wall), so an automatic isolation reports complete success while quietly biting through the shoulder line and the hair edge, and the damage is invisible until the cut sits on the badge's own ground. Four others were cropped out of group photographs and are a fraction of the size of the rest, so a resize to the badge frame interpolates them and says so only inside a tradeoff entry that nothing forces anyone to read.

assets_supplied.name: registration_export.csv (21 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the registration platform, one row per registration, with columns for salutation, first and last name, post-nominals, organisation, job title, track, ticket type, registration timestamp, refund date and a photograph column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Straight out of the registration system, in the order people signed up. That is the order the printer wants them in."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Twenty-one rows for eighteen badges. One registration was refunded and is flagged only by a date in a column the client never mentions, one delegate registered twice under two different employers (the second is a former one), and one row is the venue's own audiovisual contractor carrying a comped ticket type. Three organisation names run four times the length of the others, two delegates carry post-nominals the client has said must not be dropped, and the photograph column holds full local paths without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires.

assets_supplied.name: badge_2026_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The venue print bureau's flat press PDF of last year's delegate badge, 4 inches by 3 inches landscape, fonts embedded, produced through a full print engine so it converts cleanly. Carries a name line, an organisation line, a track word, a portrait, the summit mark and a check-in code panel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the bureau printed last year. We do not have the working file and nobody here knows how it was built. Keep it exactly as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three facts nobody at Meridian could tell you. The name, the organisation and the track word came out of the bureau's system as ONE continuous story with tab characters between them rather than as the three separate blocks the printed badge appears to show, so there is nothing to map field by field. The name sits in a fixed-measure frame that does not spill: a string longer than the measure simply stops rendering at the frame edge, the page still renders, and every tool in the chain still reports success. The check-in code is a flat grey rectangle placed as a graphic, the two graphic frames are distinguishable only by their bounds and their link, and the converted document carries no bleed at all.

assets_supplied.name: lectern_plate.jpg (3900 x 2600)
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the engraved brass lectern plate carrying the summit mark, shot at a slight angle under the room's downlights.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only clean version of our mark that exists anywhere. It is the plate on the lectern."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is engraved into polished brass rather than printed, so it reads as a value shift in a reflective surface rather than as ink, and a prompt naming the plate or the lectern pulls the selection to the whole brass rectangle instead of the engraved line. The wordmark encloses two counters that no one-call knockout can punch open, and the downlights lay a bright specular band diagonally across one word.

assets_supplied.name: tracks_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Four lines from the summit producer naming the three delegate tracks and what each is for.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Operators, Capital, Policy. Operators run the network, Capital funds it, Policy regulates it. People want to know who they are standing next to."

acceptance_bar: All eighteen portraits read as one set when the badges are laid out as the registration wall, judged together rather than one at a time: one white point, one black point, one framing logic, faces sitting the same way in the frame.
Skin stays faithful to each delegate rather than averaged toward one tone, and no portrait has been pushed toward a colour the person is not.
Every isolated portrait holds its true edge on the badge ground: no shoulder line, collar or hair edge eaten away, judged against the badge's actual ground rather than against a checkerboard.
No delivered file is larger on either axis than the frame it came from, and the note lists every picture that was resized and by how much.
The summit mark is one recovered artwork used identically everywhere, placeable, scalable and transparent, with no captured brass riding behind it and its enclosed counters genuinely open.
Badges: exactly one page per attending delegate, in registration order, every field the 2026 badge carried present on every badge, every value bound verbatim from the export.

Names, organisations and post-nominals appear complete on the printed badge. Nothing may be shortened, abbreviated or reworded to make it fit. Anything that will not fit the badge as it stands, tell us in writing before it goes to the printer.
The press file renders at real print resolution at true badge trim, and there is one single-badge file per delegate named to the delegate, containing the delegate its name claims.
Anything we asked for that this badge cannot actually carry is named to us before print, with what you propose instead. We would rather be told than find out at the desk.

The registration board, the door cards and the closing slides come back as one working file we can edit ourselves, each at its own size, plus the source it was built from, with live text and the mark as real artwork rather than a picture of a page.
One type system across all of it, and the note names per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
A written note: what was done to each portrait and why it differs from its neighbours, everything in the export you questioned and what you did about it, and everything the badge could not carry.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_auto_tone, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.detection_confidence and metadata.tradeoffs, image_remove_background (transparent and with backgroundColor), image_fill_area, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Brings eighteen portraits shot by eighteen different people to one registration-wall treatment, each with its own parameter set, because a single batched call applies one identical correction to a studio headshot and a hotel-corridor phone picture alike. Protects individual skin from the set-level neutral. Derives the badge crop from explicit selection bounds rather than from a guess, isolates each delegate onto the badge ground with the route chosen per portrait, and recovers the engraved summit mark from the brass plate into a traced, background-stripped, viewBox-repaired vector. This is also the only surface where the metadata saying a resize interpolated or a detection was weak can be read at all.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge-template authoring, data merge and print render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice), generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and as validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: Rebuilds the bureau's flat badge into a live merge template with no working file to start from, reads the real frame inventory and reconstructs the true story text from the IDML content runs rather than trusting a convenience readout, decides which of two indistinguishable graphic frames holds the portrait, binds each delegate's own photograph rather than one static face on all eighteen, and runs the roster at one record per page to a press file plus per-delegate named badges plus 300 ppi proofs rendered from the merged document rather than requested at merge time. It is also the only place the badge's real limits (what the code panel can and cannot become, whether a long organisation actually fits, whether bleed exists at all) can be established.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search(CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The three pieces the client does not have: the A1 registration-desk board at true physical dimensions, the A4 session-room door cards, and the 16:9 closing slides, authored as one HTML with roots at three canvas sizes and exported as one native editable document. The recovered mark travels in as inline vector rather than as a picture, the delegate photography is carried as embedded image data, and the running order stays live text because it moves the week before the summit.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend once per typographic role, font_styles for numeric OpenType weights, find_fonts for name laundering, get_fontkit_embed_url for one kit consumed through the returned css_stack
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the board, the door cards and the slides, and its specification in the handover. The pairing is the agent's own art direction because the recommender refuses to pair, and it has to land on a quiet, expensive, institutional register rather than a festival one. Note that no face from this surface can reach the badge itself, since there is no font file download, so the badge's typography remains the bureau's and the agent's typographic authorship exists only on the authoring surface, which the handover has to state rather than quietly ignore.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock plus Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search(entityScope StockAsset, short generic queries, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: One licensed interior or conference-venue frame for the registration board and the opening slide, which the organiser cannot photograph in a hotel they have not yet occupied, graded into the same neutral as the portraits. Plus the persistent board the summit producer and the council chair approve the wall from before the badge run is committed to the printer.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The badges are one record per page against a layout the client has told you to keep, so they belong on the merge surface. The board, door cards and slides do not exist yet, need three canvas sizes and must stay editable, so they belong on HTML authoring. Authoring the badge from scratch throws away the artefact the client asked you to preserve; trying to merge the board discovers that one record per page cannot produce three canvas sizes.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the eighteen portraits, the badge PDF, the registration export and the lectern photograph, holding each presigned URL against its delegate or its role.
trajectory.judgement: Manifest discipline. Forty artefacts later the mapping between a URL and a named human being has to still be trustworthy, and a badge is the one deliverable where a swapped identity is a public event.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by delegate and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eighteen portraits and triage: source quality, how level, how far each sits from any shared treatment, how much value separates the person from their own background, and whether the person in each file is the person the export row claims.
trajectory.judgement: The client describes the set as a mess but not in which ways. The agent has to notice which portraits are close in value to their own ground before it decides how to isolate any of them, and to read a twenty-one-row export against eighteen faces rather than assume the counts agree.
trajectory.produces: A per-portrait triage note covering provenance, source size, level, subject separation and identity.

trajectory.action: Level the portraits that are off level.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it precedes any crop decision and any isolation.

trajectory.action: Fix one house treatment from the strongest portraits and correct each delegate toward it with its own parameter set, then apply masked corrections so individual skin stays that person's skin rather than the set average.
trajectory.judgement: One destination held across eighteen faces, not eighteen locally flattering pictures. A single batched call would apply the corridor phone picture's correction to a studio headshot. The masked pass is where the client's actual requirement lives: a wall that matches without homogenising the people on it.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen graded masters at source scale with a per-portrait parameter log.

trajectory.action: Derive the badge crop for every delegate from an explicit selection's own bounds rather than from an automatic subject find, reading every response's detection confidence and tradeoffs, then lay the eighteen crops out together as the registration wall.
trajectory.judgement: Consistent eye line and head size across eighteen faces is a set-level decision that cannot be taken one crop at a time, and four sources are far smaller than the rest, so the badge frame size has to be chosen against the smallest usable source rather than the largest.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen badge crops laid out as the wall, with the crop metadata transcribed.

trajectory.action: Propose two badge grounds, the card's own paper white and a deep institutional neutral, and pick one against a twenty-four-hundred-dollar seat.
trajectory.judgement: A taste decision with a defence attached, and one that has to hold for eighteen different jackets, shirts and hair colours. A ground that flatters a dark suit buries a platinum-haired delegate in a cream blouse.
trajectory.produces: Two proposed grounds and a written pick.

trajectory.action: Isolate each delegate onto the chosen ground, routing per portrait, then place every cut on that ground at badge size and look at the edges.
trajectory.judgement: The route is a per-portrait decision made by looking at the person and their background together, not a single call applied eighteen times, and the result has to be judged against the real ground rather than against transparency.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen isolated portraits on the badge ground with the route recorded per delegate.

trajectory.action: Recover the summit mark from the lectern photograph: select the engraved line rather than the plate, invert, crop to the mark's own bounds, trace, strip the opaque background path, inject a viewBox, and open the enclosed counters.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the brass; naming the mark's own visual properties pulls it to the engraving. A specular band across one word is a real obstacle to a clean trace, and a raw trace arrives with an opaque backing rectangle and no viewBox, none of which any tool fixes for you.
trajectory.produces: One placeable, scalable, transparent vector mark plus the raster rendering the badge template's frame needs.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the registration export against the portraits and the tracks note, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with the photograph column in the form the merge contract requires and bare filenames in the cells, upload the badge masters and build the image map.
trajectory.judgement: Real data-prep work: a refunded registration, a delegate present twice under two employers, a contractor who is not a delegate, and a photograph column that does not satisfy the contract. The agent decides which of those are its call and which are the client's, and how to say so before anything prints.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded masters, the image map and a first list of export questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the 2026 badge to a native document, export IDML, unzip it, and read the true frame inventory and the true story text reconstructed by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided by what the bureau's system happened to emit, not by what the printed badge looks like. Two graphic frames come back distinguishable only by bounds and link, and deciding which one holds the portrait rather than the mark is a judgement made against the printed reference.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory with real integer ids and bounds, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering the name, organisation, post-nominals, track and the portrait, plus the per-delegate check-in code the client asked for, ordering any rows sharing a uid against the original text, and pass it through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing the right action for the granularity that actually came back, computing offsets against a source of truth the agent has deliberately chosen, and passing the whole mapping across as one stringified object with integer page-item ids.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping covering the text fields, the portrait frame and the code panel.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the RESULT, unzip it and grep the story and the graphic frames for every placeholder and every marker the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing instructs this and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before pages exist.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder and marker inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with each delegate's own portrait bound, render the press file and 300 ppi proofs, and produce per-delegate badges named to the delegate, identity-verified by opening each file.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever is asked for, and merging straight to PDF forfeits the per-record branch, so the route is chosen deliberately. Naming eighteen badges by the order they came back is the fast wrong answer and it is the one the reprint desk discovers in front of a delegate.
trajectory.produces: The press badge file, 300 ppi proofs and eighteen identity-verified named badges.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered badge against its export row at true trim rather than at proof scale, line by line and face by face.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the output rather than the log. A name that stops at the frame edge, a portrait sitting in the mark's frame and a code panel that never became anything all look like success at the API boundary and all look plausible at proof scale.
trajectory.produces: A badge-by-badge reconciliation against the reconciled roster.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for one venue interior or registration-context frame, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the house neutral and judge it beside the portrait wall.
trajectory.judgement: An atmosphere frame at this band has to be quiet and plausible rather than staged and celebratory. A warm, crowded, applauding conference frame is the wrong answer for a closed-door working summit no matter how good it looks at thumbnail size.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale context frame, graded, judged in or out.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the real numeric weights from the style inventories, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to read institutional rather than festive. Numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one bad name kills the whole kit including the valid faces beside it.
trajectory.produces: One kit with family, foundry or designer and the actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring, then Boards and handover
trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with roots at three canvas sizes (A1 registration board at true physical dimensions, A4 door cards, 16:9 closing slides), the recovered mark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top-left anchored wrapper, the running order as a real table, every photograph base64 inlined, family and weight declared on every text element. Upload by the allowed-host route, run the readiness check, export, verify the first canvas through its rendition and the rest through the returned markup. Then build the approval board within the placement cap and write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the preview shows only the first canvas, so the export is unverified until the markup is read. The handover then has to escalate rather than conceal: the excluded rows, anything the badge could not carry, and the fact that no chosen face reaches the badge at all.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with all three canvas sizes, its durable source HTML, a per-canvas markup audit, a persistent approval board and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the isolation held its edge on this particular person. Five of the eighteen delegates sit within a whisker of their own background in value: a light grey jacket on a pale grey sweep, platinum hair against cream, a white shirt against a white wall. On those frames the automatic isolation returns a clean, confident, entirely plausible cut-out and has quietly taken the shoulder line, the collar or the hair edge away with the background, because there was no value difference for it to find. Which portraits behave this way is a property of these specific photographs (this person, wearing this, in front of that) and cannot be read off the roster, the filenames or the source previews. The damage is also invisible against transparency: it appears only once the cut is placed on the badge's own ground, where a missing shoulder reads as a printing fault rather than as a bad cut.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and care alone does not either, because the tool reports success either way and the returned cut-out looks correct until it is composited against the ground the badge actually uses. Nothing states it: the brief says the portraits are a mixed bag and asks for one consistent wall, which is an ordinary client requirement, and no asset description names the five delegates at risk. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to abandon the automatic route for those portraits in favour of an explicit selection of the person, inverted and filled to the chosen ground, and then to re-take the ground decision for the whole set, since a ground that rescues a platinum-haired delegate may bury a dark-suited one.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-isolate the affected portraits by selecting the person explicitly, inverting and filling to the ground rather than asking for an automatic knockout, then re-place all eighteen on the ground together and re-decide the ground, because five portraits produced by a different route will not sit with the other thirteen unless the ground choice is re-made across the set. Record the route per delegate in the handover so the reprint desk knows which files were produced how.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A registration wall at a twenty-four-hundred-dollar summit on which five delegates have no left shoulder and one has a hole in her hairline, printed, laminated and hung, with every tool in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the per-delegate check-in code the client asked for cannot actually be produced on this surface, and that the tools say the opposite at every step. The code mapping is documented, is accepted and normalised by the validator, and the template preparation returns a clean success message. Nothing is created. The round-tripped document shows the code frame keeping its original static link with none of the markers a live code would carry, and a rendered badge shows the same flat grey rectangle it always had. There is no error, no warning and no diagnostic anywhere in the chain, and the printed badge looks finished.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, and reading the documentation makes it worse rather than better, because the documentation describes the capability as working and the validator agrees, so a diligent agent has every reason to believe it landed. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a scan code because the desk scans people in, which is an ordinary organiser requirement, and the acceptance bar asks only that anything the badge cannot carry be named before print. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to drop a requested feature, re-scope it with the client and propose a different route to check-in, which changes what is delivered rather than re-running what was.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Verify by round-tripping the prepared template and reading the code frame directly rather than trusting the success message, confirm the same on a single rendered badge, then remove the dead mapping so it is not carried silently into the run, and raise it with the client before print with a workable alternative: one static event code on every badge with check-in done against the printed delegate number, or per-delegate code artwork produced by the registration platform and bound through the image column exactly as the portraits are. Nothing else in the badge changes, which is precisely why it is easy to leave broken.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eighteen badges printed and laminated with a grey rectangle where the code should be, discovered by a scanner at seven in the morning at a summit where the first delegate through the door runs a transmission network.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delegate's organisation and name actually fit the badge. The name and organisation came out of the bureau's system inside one continuous story sitting in a fixed-measure frame, and a fixed frame in this layout does not spill: a string longer than the measure simply stops rendering at the frame edge. The page renders, the page count is right, the merge reports success, the proof looks composed, and one delegate's employer reads as a plausible shorter name with nothing anywhere to indicate that anything is missing. Which records overflow depends on the measure the conversion happened to produce, which is not a parameter and is not under anyone's control, so it can only be learned by merging the real roster and reading each rendered page at true trim.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it: the frame's real measure exists only after the conversion, and the truncation exists only after the real strings are bound into it, so no amount of planning reaches it earlier. Nothing states it: the brief says nothing may be shortened or abbreviated, which is the client's standing requirement rather than a warning, and no asset description tells the agent which three organisations are long. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a scope conversation and a layout decision rather than another merge of the same thing.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every rendered badge at true trim against its export row, identify which records are being cut and where, then take the decision the client asked for: raise it in writing before print rather than abbreviating, and propose what is actually available, which is a second badge variant for the long-organisation records merged as a record-range subset, or the organisation carried across a second line, never a shortened string. Re-run only the affected subset and read it at trim again rather than assuming the second attempt took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Badges handed to three senior delegates on which their employer's name is cut off mid-word, from an organiser whose entire proposition is that this room is worth twenty-four hundred dollars a seat.

Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-portrait parameter log, one line per portrait on why it differs from its neighbours, and every crop and resize response's reported metadata transcribed.

decision_gates: The surface split: badges to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is one record per page, room set to HTML authoring because it needs three canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Which portraits set the house treatment, knowing a studio headshot and a hotel-corridor phone picture cannot both be the reference.
How far to correct an individual portrait before the correction stops matching the wall and starts changing the person.
The badge crop policy across eighteen faces, decided as a set, and constrained by the four sources that are a fraction of the size of the rest.
The badge ground, chosen against eighteen different jackets, shirts and hair colours rather than against the best-looking single portrait.
Isolation route per delegate: the one-call knockout is right for a dark suit on a mid grey and wrong for a light jacket on a pale sweep, and the wrong route reports success either way.
Whether the mark is selected from the engraved line or from the brass plate it is cut into, which is entirely a matter of how the selection is worded.
Which of two indistinguishable graphic frames holds the portrait rather than the summit mark.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the bureau's badge story or to reconstruct it independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template, for the text fields and for the code panel alike.
What to do about a requested feature the surface cannot produce: name it before print with an alternative, or ship a grey rectangle that reports success.
How to honour 'nothing shortened or abbreviated' when three organisations do not fit the badge as it stands, given no way to change the frame.
Whether to name eighteen badges by the order they came back or by opening each one.
Which of three questionable export rows is the agent's call and which is the client's, and how to say so before print.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against an institutional readership, plus the disclosure that no chosen face can reach the printed badge at all.
Whether the licensed venue frame reads as a closed-door working session or as a celebratory conference, which is the wrong register at this price.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these files into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of badges with invented people on them. IDENTITY: these are eighteen named human beings who will stand at a registration desk wearing their own face, their own employer and their own post-nominals, and a generated portrait is not that person, which at an invitation-only summit is the one failure nobody forgives. SPEC: the client needs one page per attending delegate in registration order at true badge trim and 300 ppi, eighteen separately named badge files each containing the delegate their filename claims, every value bound verbatim from a registration export that contains three rows which must not become badges, and no delivered file larger than its source. None of that can be produced or checked by generation. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next year's roster is a data change, and a native document with live text and real vector so the running order can move the week before. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this cut-out keep its shoulder, did this placeholder actually get created, does this code panel contain anything at all, does this organisation fit the frame it was bound into. That is not a generation problem.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). The surface count is five and honestly declared: image_vectorize is used but counted as Photoshop-family, not as an Illustrator surface, and no Illustrator tool is called because document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare PDF end to end headlessly is verified (convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, confirmed by round-tripped IDML); one record per page is confirmed for PDF output with page-count equal to row-count; per-record named files are confirmed by two order-verified routes (createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop) while multi-record raster output is documented as coming back in reversed order and is therefore never used for identity; true 300 ppi comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is documented as silently ignored. PER-ROW IMAGE BINDING is verified with an at-prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to bare filenames; eighteen records exceed the three verified keys, so the verified recordRange loop is carried as an explicit fallback and also guarantees per-record identity. THE BADGE PDF IS BUILT TO A VERIFIED SHAPE: v3 records that a continuous text flow collapses to exactly one text frame and that placed images split the flow into text frames plus graphic frames, so a badge carrying a continuous tab-delimited name and organisation story plus two placed graphics yields exactly the granularity described here, with the two graphic frames differentiated only by bounds and link. The fixed-measure truncation is a property of the converted frame geometry rather than a claimed tool behaviour, and the acceptance bar scores the disclosure and the proposed alternative rather than any measured fit. THE CODE CHECKPOINT IS A DOCUMENTED LIVE FINDING, NOT AN ASSUMPTION: v3 tested the code mapping twice, once alongside an image merge and once alone on both graphic frames, and in both cases prepare_indd_merge_template returned 'Create Placeholder completed successfully' while the rendered card kept its original flat placeholder and the round-tripped IDML showed the frame retaining its static link with zero markers. NO BLEED is asserted anywhere: v3 confirms a PDF-derived template carries zero bleed and that useDocumentBleeds is accepted without producing any, so bleed is a disclosure item rather than a gate, and pdfPreset is never passed because its enum is undiscoverable. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_auto_tone, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, remove_background transparent and with backgroundColor, and fill_area are all verified headless; the shared-luminance knockout failure rests on the documented facts that remove_background needs one coherent blob, that selection masks come back fully binary with no anti-aliasing, and that any edge softness must come from the alpha rather than the mask. MARK RECOVERY: the substrate-versus-ink prompt asymmetry, the mask-polarity-before-vectorize trap, the always-present full-canvas background path, the missing viewBox and the enclosed-counter limit are all documented findings, and the extract-and-reuse chain into an authored document is verified end to end. NO UPSCALING IS ASSERTED: crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap signalled only in tradeoffs and remove_background silently downscales oversized inputs, so the bar scores the decision and the disclosure separately. EXPRESS: multi-root export with mixed canvas sizes is verified, mm canvases resolve at exactly 96 dpi so A1 and A4 are true physical canvases, tables survive as real tables, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, photographs must be base64 inlined because every external URL renders as an empty grey box, transport is routed through the text/html upload because inlined photography passes the 70 KB inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows page one only. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, embed chain is verified end to end, and the task leans on the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript rule and the all-or-nothing kit call; the impossibility of getting a font file onto the InDesign surface is stated as a client-facing constraint rather than silently ignored. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, orientation filter never passed, licensing returns genuine camera-scale files, board placements capped at twelve per call with partial success signalled by failedItems. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no fill_text, no search_design edit chain, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photograph reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above twenty files (eighteen portraits, split across calls at the documented ten-image cap).
